items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: There was one of George Williams that played in Handy up in Memphis.

ctx.x: I don't know, I take my liking to trombone. There was a show that came into New Orleans, and they had two trombones. And I noticed a fellow that was playing trombone. He was quick and fast, and he could handle that trombone faster. Well, when I first started, I told fellows I was going to imitate that fellow. And they tried to disgust me. They said, you'll never play like that fellow. They said, you'll never play like that fellow. I said, well, I don't know, I'm going to try. And I kept trying and doing it wrong.…
There was one of George Williams that played in Handy up in Memphis.

Yeah. That's the same fellow, yeah. He's wonderful. He could do more with a trombone, I don't know, backwards, you know what you could say. I would play forwards, see. I practiced all that, but I never used it much, you know, but I knew it, you know. Practicing how you can find these trombone players now, they don't use backwards, you know, like that. All they know is what, forward, back, like that. But not playing back down, going down this way, they don't know nothing about that. Didn't that string? Lower…
